name: Coverage

subjectOf.text: Possibility-space quality is captured by four functionals, coverage, precision, robustness, and calibration, and value in Computative Economics derives from their composite rather than from any single dimension.
subjectOf.abstract: Calibration measures the alignment between the generation function's internal quality estimates and verified external performance. Value in Computative Economics derives from the composite of these dimensions rather than from any single one.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Computative Economics A Framework for Economic Analysis under Computational Abundance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6607458

subjectOf.text: The expected coverage of the joint possibility space generated by n agents under the composition operator strictly exceeds the expected coverage of the union of their individual possibility spaces whenever at least one quality dimension is super-additive in agent collaboration.
subjectOf.abstract: The expected coverage of the joint possibility space generated by n agents under the composition operator Φ strictly exceeds the expected coverage of the union of their individual possibility spaces, when at least one quality dimension is super-additive in agent collaboration.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
scope_conditions: at least one quality dimension is super-additive in collaboration

subjectOf.text: No validator, filter, or score in the design is asked about rarity, novelty, frequency, diversity, or coverage, and the outcome is computed by an evaluator alone from a sealed reference that no filter reads.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The oracle alone receives one bit per candidate from the sealed reference, the candidate's true validity verdict.
Validators do see a tag, whose association with rare membership is bounded by design.
